answer: By modeling trust propagation via personalized EigenTrust matrices, we prove that spectral partition barriers isolate adversarial clusters. When an attacker triggers a sybil spiral to breach these limits, a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function imposes sequentially bound steps. Coupled with slashing penalties on velvet staking collateral, this constraint forces the expected utility of generating a plume of fake identities to be strictly negative, yielding a robust, collusion-resistant Nash equilibrium.
